subject: SilverOak integration — function-calling & routing POC scope
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika@silveroak.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: SilverOak integration — function-calling & routing POC scope

Hi Anika — thanks again for the discovery call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed POC scope focused on the function/tool-calling and routing pieces we discussed. TL;DR: two-phase POC (hosted de-id dataset -> private/VPC pilot), function-definition-first approach, and a fail-open fallback strategy for routing.

Recap of key constraints you mentioned:
- No PHI leaving customer boundary for pilot (strict requirement)
- Need sub-300ms median tail for short lookups where possible
- High QPS for reranker stage on catalog search (100+ QPS expected)

Proposed integration pattern (high-level):
1) SDK & auth:
   - Use Redwood SDK (JS/Go) for request plumbing. Auth via short-lived service tokens (we can mint with your KMS or provide token broker for hosted).
   - For Private/VPC, we recommend service-account credentials with rotating keys + KMS-managed envelope encryption.
2) Tool/function calling model:
   - Define canonical function defs for external actions (examples attached in fn-defs-v1.yaml): product_lookup(id), price_estimate(context), invoice_fetch(order_id). Each definition includes: input schema, timeout/backoff, idempotency-key, and allowed call destinations.
   - Execution modes: (A) webhook callbacks to your infra, (B) connector that executes functions inside your VPC (preferred for PHI).
3) Parallelism & error handling:
   - Parallel fan-out for independent tools (race-first-success with quorum where applicable).
   - Circuit breaker around external tool endpoints, exponential backoff + jitter, and explicit fallbacks to cached results or degraded UX templates.
   - Idempotency tokens for at-most-once semantics for stateful actions.
4) Routing & model fallbacks:
   - Primary routing: hosted lowest-cost variant (when allowed). Fallbacks: Dedicated pool in us-west, then private connector for critical PHI calls.
   - Policy-driven: route by data sensitivity tag + SLO requirement.
5) Embeddings & rerank pipeline:
   - Use Redwood embeddings service for candidate encoding -> approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) + optional BM25 hybrid.
   - Reranker as a fast two-stage: coarse embedding similarity to shortlist, then model-based score for final ordering. Keep candidate cutoff configurable (e.g., 200 -> 50 -> top N).

POC proposal (2 weeks):
- Week 1: implement function-defs, hosted SDK integration with de-identified sample dataset, baseline rerank pipeline, run latency and throughput numbers.
- Week 2: security review, connector tech spike for VPC execution, and run smoke tests with your sample workload.

Deliverables we will provide: function-definition YAML, architecture diagram (attached), sample benchmarking harness, and a short QA checklist for security. Attachments: fn-defs-v1.yaml, architecture-diagram.png.

Asks from your side: de-identified sample dataset (CSV of catalog + queries), contact for infra/Sec (for VPC options), and a staging AWS account if we go private connector path.

Proposed next meeting: Thu Nov 12, 10:00 AM PT — 30 min technical deep-dive. Is that ok?

Thanks — happy to adjust scope based on your risk posture.

--
Diego Fernandez
Integrations Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0191

From: Anika Shah <anika@silveroak.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mohammad Rahman <mohammad@silveroak.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SilverOak integration — function-calling & routing POC scope

Thanks Diego — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing:

1) PHI/data residency:
   - For the initial POC we cannot send any PHI to hosted systems. We can provide a de-identified catalog but any production pilot must run in our VPC or on-prem. Please confirm the connector option can run entirely within our VPC and that function payloads will not be brokered through public endpoints.
2) Security/compliance artifacts:
   - Please share SOC2 certification and relevant audit logs capability. If there is a BAA/BAA-forwarding process at Redwood, flag it — compliance will need internal review.
3) Latency & rerank throughput:
   - For the catalog use-case we expect bursts to 120 QPS with 50ms P50 and <= 300ms P95 for short retrievals. For the rerank stage, we expect batching and GPU-backed inference. Can you share benchmark profiles (tokens per request, latency by model family) we can compare?
4) Tool trust boundary:
   - We prefer function execution inside our network for anything that touches customer data. If hosted callbacks are required, they must be encrypted at rest/in-flight and we need the option to redact responses before they leave our network.

We will attach a sample dataset (sample-catalog.csv) and loop in Mohammad (sec/infra). Mohammad will lead the technical deep-dive. Nov 13 at 11:00 AM PT works better for us than Nov 12.

Also: can you confirm cost expectations for running reranker at scale (ballpark monthly units)? That will feed into procurement planning.

Regards,
Anika Shah
Head of Engineering | SilverOak AI
anika@silveroak.ai
+1 (650) 555-2410

Attachment: sample-catalog.csv

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika@silveroak.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SilverOak integration — function-calling & routing POC scope

Anika — great, thanks for the fast clarifications and the sample dataset. Quick responses to your bullets and an updated, constrained plan: 

1) Connector / VPC execution:
   - Yes — connector option can execute functions inside your VPC (we deploy a lightweight container + controller that runs in your subnet; outbound control is zero by default). That means function payloads never hit Redwood-hosted runtime for sensitive calls. We documented the two modes in the attached architecture diagram (edge connector vs hosted webhook).
2) Compliance artifacts:
   - I'm attaching a link to our SOC 2 summary in the Drive link; we can provide the full SOC report under an NDA. We do support BAAs for enterprise customers — Marissa will coordinate legal.
3) Latency/benchmarks & rerank economics:
   - Baseline numbers (hosted, nv4-like GPU): P50 ~ 40-60ms for short model calls (small context), P95 ~ 220-300ms depending on batch sizing. Reranker throughput: expect GPU throughput ~ 80-200 QPS depending on candidate set and batching. We'll run a targeted benchmark with your sample dataset.
   - Cost: rough hosted estimate for rerank stage (embedding + reranker) for your expected QPS is in the proposal we'll give during the procurement chat — Marissa will prepare a ballpark.
4) Data protections & redaction:
   - For hosted POCs we can integrate a pre-send redaction/masking hook in your client or connector; for private mode this is unnecessary since calls stay internal.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm Nov 13 11:00 AM PT for the technical deep-dive (Mohammad + infra team).
- Marissa to share the function-definition template + preliminary cost ballpark prior to the call.
- Sean to own the benchmark harness and schedule a 2-day run after the deep-dive.

If this looks good I will send a short agenda for Nov 13 and create a HubSpot entry for the POC milestones (I already created the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890).

Thanks — looping Marissa and Sean to assign tasks.

--
Diego Fernandez
Integrations Engineer | Redwood Inference
